hypothesis: If AVGO preserves its current trailing free-cash-flow valuation premium to NVDA at the terminal date, the AVGO 10% post-FY2028 growth probability required to match NVDA falls materially from the equal-terminal-multiple hurdle of 96.25978682%.

decision_rule.condition: Use only as a terminal-multiple sensitivity, not as a probability estimate. CONDITION if current relative trailing FCF multiple changes the required AVGO growth-scenario probability by at least 10 percentage points versus the equal-multiple canonical benchmark; otherwise REJECT.

NVDA.source: NVIDIA FY2026 and Q2 FY2027 results / SEC filings

AVGO.calculation: FY2025 FCF 26.914 - first nine months FY2025 FCF 19.448 + first nine months FY2026 FCF 31.937
AVGO.source: Broadcom FY2025 and Q3 FY2026 results / SEC filings

relative_multiple_sensitivity.assumption: At the terminal date AVGO Price/FCF is 1.05807215 times NVDA Price/FCF, equal to the observed trailing relative multiple at this as-of state.

benchmark_and_alternative.benchmark: Equal AVGO/NVDA terminal Price/FCF multiple: required probability 96.25978682%.
benchmark_and_alternative.alternative: Preserve observed AVGO/NVDA trailing Price/FCF ratio 1.05807215 at terminal: required probability 76.10409619%.
benchmark_and_alternative.result: The terminal-relative-multiple assumption changes the hurdle by 20.15569063 percentage points, exceeding the pre-specified 10-point materiality threshold.

usage_rule: CONDITION. Treat 96.25978682% as conditional on equal terminal multiples, not as a model-independent AVGO probability hurdle. Do not use 76.10409619% as a forecast probability. Use this artifact to require explicit relative-terminal-multiple sensitivity in AVGO/NVDA capital-allocation decisions until a point-in-time historical multiple distribution is validated.

risk_metrics.reason: This is a valuation sensitivity study, not a realized return-series strategy backtest.

limitations: Current trailing Price/FCF is not evidence that the same relative multiple will persist five years forward.

Per-share trailing FCF uses the latest reported diluted weighted-average shares rather than an exact current basic share count, so the observed relative multiple is a valuation sensitivity input, not a canonical market-cap multiple.
NVIDIA and Broadcom define/report free cash flow on issuer-specific bases; the calculation uses each issuer's reported FCF and does not claim perfect accounting comparability.
No historical point-in-time relative multiple distribution has yet been validated, so this result cannot set the canonical terminal multiple.
next_research: Build point-in-time annual AVGO and NVDA Price/FCF distributions using contemporaneous issuer-reported FCF and share counts, then test whether the relative terminal multiple ratio has a stable out-of-sample range.
